questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The term ‘accounting period’ is used to refer to the

options.A: time span during which taxes are paid to the Inland Revenue Board
options.B: Budget period, usually one year, relied on by the accountant
options.C: time span, usually one year covered by financial statement
options.D: period within which debtors are expected to settle accounts.

questions.ai_explanation: An accounting period is the reporting interval covered by financial statements. It is commonly one year, allowing performance for that interval to be measured.
questions.explanation: An accounting period is the reporting interval covered by financial statements. It is commonly one year, allowing performance for that interval to be measured.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following factors’ has aided the development of Accounting?

options.B: The discovery of mineral resources in commercial quantity.
options.C: The growth in size of businesses and the separation of ownership and management.
options.D: The development and management of a sophisticated monetary system.

questions.ai_explanation: As businesses grow and owners delegate management, formal accounts allow managers to report how resources were used and owners to assess that performance.
questions.explanation: As businesses grow and owners delegate management, formal accounts allow managers to report how resources were used and owners to assess that performance.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Assigning revenues to the accounting period in which goods were sold or services rendered and expenses incurred is known as
questions.ai_explanation: The matching concept relates expenses to the revenue they helped generate in the same accounting period, allowing the profit for that period to be measured.
questions.explanation: The matching concept relates expenses to the revenue they helped generate in the same accounting period, allowing the profit for that period to be measured.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The accounting convention which states that ‘profit must not be recognized until realized while all losses should be adequately provided for’ is termed
questions.ai_explanation: Conservatism, also called prudence in traditional accounting terminology, requires caution when recognising uncertain gains and providing for expected losses.
questions.explanation: Conservatism, also called prudence in traditional accounting terminology, requires caution when recognising uncertain gains and providing for expected losses.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An effective accounting system should provide information

options.C: on internal and external reporting for managers and third parties
options.D: for promoters, directors, labour unions and distributors.

questions.ai_explanation: An accounting system supports internal management decisions and external reporting. Its information serves managers as well as users outside the organisation.
questions.explanation: An accounting system supports internal management decisions and external reporting. Its information serves managers as well as users outside the organisation.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Accounting information is used by investors and creditors of a company to predict

options.A: future cash flows of the company
options.B: future tax payments of the company
options.C: potential merger candidates for the company
options.D: appropriate remuneration for the company’s staff.

questions.ai_explanation: Investors and creditors assess the amounts, timing and uncertainty of future cash flows. Those flows affect the business’s ability to provide returns and repay obligations.
questions.explanation: Investors and creditors assess the amounts, timing and uncertainty of future cash flows. Those flows affect the business’s ability to provide returns and repay obligations.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When a business incurs labours cost in installing a fixed asset, the cost is treated as
questions.ai_explanation: Labour directly attributable to bringing a fixed asset into working condition forms part of its cost. Installation labour is therefore added to the asset rather than expensed as routine wages.
questions.explanation: Labour directly attributable to bringing a fixed asset into working condition forms part of its cost. Installation labour is therefore added to the asset rather than expensed as routine wages.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Malam Gambo bought a freezer for his shop costing N 10,500. In recording, he debited office expenses account and credited the bank account. What book keeping error has he committed?
questions.ai_explanation: A freezer used in the shop is a capital asset. Charging its purchase to office expenses wrongly treats capital expenditure as revenue expenditure, which is an error of principle.
questions.explanation: A freezer used in the shop is a capital asset. Charging its purchase to office expenses wrongly treats capital expenditure as revenue expenditure, which is an error of principle.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The use of the folio in the ledger is for
questions.ai_explanation: A folio is a cross-reference to the related book or account page. It helps trace the posting back to its source and locate the corresponding entry.
questions.explanation: A folio is a cross-reference to the related book or account page. It helps trace the posting back to its source and locate the corresponding entry.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Tanko’s account has debits: opening balance ₦5,000 and sales ₦10,000; credits: cash ₦3,000 and bank ₦6,500. What is the closing balance amount?
questions.ai_explanation: Debits total ₦5,000 + ₦10,000 = ₦15,000. Credits total ₦3,000 + ₦6,500 = ₦9,500. Their difference is a closing debit balance of ₦5,500.
questions.explanation: Debits total ₦5,000 + ₦10,000 = ₦15,000. Credits total ₦3,000 + ₦6,500 = ₦9,500. Their difference is a closing debit balance of ₦5,500.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When is a petty cash account debited?

options.A: When the fund is established and every time money is spent
options.B: when the fund is established and every time it is replenished
options.C: when the fund is established and when the size of the float is decreased
options.D: Every time money is drawn from the petty cash.

questions.ai_explanation: Petty cash is an asset. Establishing or replenishing the fund increases that asset and is recorded as a debit; spending from it is recorded as a credit.
questions.explanation: Petty cash is an asset. Establishing or replenishing the fund increases that asset and is recorded as a debit; spending from it is recorded as a credit.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When reconciling a positive balance per bank statement to the cash-book balance, which item is deducted?
questions.ai_explanation: An unpresented cheque is already deducted in the cash book but has not yet reduced the bank statement balance. Deduct it when reconciling a positive bank-statement balance to the cash-book balance.
questions.explanation: An unpresented cheque is already deducted in the cash book but has not yet reduced the bank statement balance. Deduct it when reconciling a positive bank-statement balance to the cash-book balance.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The financial position of an organization at a particular time can be ascertained from the

options.A: statement of sources and application of funds

questions.ai_explanation: The balance sheet, or statement of financial position, reports assets, liabilities and equity at a specified date. Profit and loss instead reports performance over a period.
questions.explanation: The balance sheet, or statement of financial position, reports assets, liabilities and equity at a specified date. Profit and loss instead reports performance over a period.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Purchases are ₦20,000; sales ₦40,000; carriage inwards ₦5,000; carriage outwards ₦5,000; opening stock ₦10,000; closing stock ₦5,000. Find cost of goods sold.
questions.ai_explanation: Cost of goods sold is opening stock plus purchases and carriage inwards, less closing stock: ₦10,000 + ₦20,000 + ₦5,000 − ₦5,000 = ₦30,000. Carriage outwards is a selling expense.
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold is opening stock plus purchases and carriage inwards, less closing stock: ₦10,000 + ₦20,000 + ₦5,000 − ₦5,000 = ₦30,000. Carriage outwards is a selling expense.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The net profit or loss for the year is determined in the profit and loss account after

options.B: Deducting cost of goods sold from sales and adding administrative expenses
options.C: Adding commissions received to gross profit
options.D: Deducting all operating expenses from gross profit and adding other income

questions.ai_explanation: Net profit is gross profit plus other income less operating expenses. Purchases alone do not represent all costs, and administrative expenses must be deducted rather than added.
questions.explanation: Net profit is gross profit plus other income less operating expenses. Purchases alone do not represent all costs, and administrative expenses must be deducted rather than added.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening stock:3,000 units at ₦3; January purchases:15,000 at ₦3.50; February purchases:25,000 at ₦4. January sales:13,000 at ₦4.50; February sales:28,000 at ₦5. Using LIFO, find closing stock value.
questions.ai_explanation: Total units available are 43,000 and units sold are 41,000, leaving 2,000. Under the stated LIFO exercise, the remaining units come from the opening layer at ₦3, valued at ₦6,000.
questions.explanation: Total units available are 43,000 and units sold are 41,000, leaving 2,000. Under the stated LIFO exercise, the remaining units come from the opening layer at ₦3, valued at ₦6,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening stock:3,000 units at ₦3; January purchases:15,000 at ₦3.50; February purchases:25,000 at ₦4. January sales:13,000 at ₦4.50; February sales:28,000 at ₦5. If closing stock is valued at ₦20,000, calculate gross profit at the end of February.
questions.ai_explanation: Sales total ₦198,500. Goods available cost ₦161,500; with the specified closing value ₦20,000, cost of sales is ₦141,500. Gross profit is ₦198,500 − ₦141,500 = ₦57,000.
questions.explanation: Sales total ₦198,500. Goods available cost ₦161,500; with the specified closing value ₦20,000, cost of sales is ₦141,500. Gross profit is ₦198,500 − ₦141,500 = ₦57,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: If a bad debt previously written off is subsequently repaid, the amount collected is recorded as an

options.A: income in the profit and loss account
options.C: addition cash in the profit and loss account

questions.ai_explanation: Recovery of a debt previously written off is recognised as income in the profit and loss account. The receipt also increases cash or bank in the accounting records.
questions.explanation: Recovery of a debt previously written off is recognised as income in the profit and loss account. The receipt also increases cash or bank in the accounting records.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening and closing accounts receivable are ₦8,000 and ₦15,000. Customer collections are ₦36,000. With no other receivable movements, find credit sales.
questions.ai_explanation: Opening receivables plus credit sales less collections equals closing receivables. Thus credit sales = ₦15,000 − ₦8,000 + ₦36,000 = ₦43,000.
questions.explanation: Opening receivables plus credit sales less collections equals closing receivables. Thus credit sales = ₦15,000 − ₦8,000 + ₦36,000 = ₦43,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which labour cost is classified as direct production labour?
questions.ai_explanation: Direct labour is work that can be traced to making the product. Production workers’ wages are the direct-labour category here, unlike administrative and cashier salaries.
questions.explanation: Direct labour is work that can be traced to making the product. Production workers’ wages are the direct-labour category here, unlike administrative and cashier salaries.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Inventory transactions in order: opening20units at₦6; sell18; buy30at₦8; sell20; buy10at₦9. Using FIFO, find ending inventory cost.
questions.ai_explanation: The business has 22 units remaining. FIFO leaves the latest 10 units at ₦9 and 12 units at ₦8, giving ₦90 + ₦96 = ₦186.
questions.explanation: The business has 22 units remaining. FIFO leaves the latest 10 units at ₦9 and 12 units at ₦8, giving ₦90 + ₦96 = ₦186.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The major difference between the receipt and payment account and the income and expenditure account is that while the former

options.A: The former is kept by the treasurer, the latter is not
options.B: The former records all cash received and paid during the year; the latter records income and expenses relating to that year
options.C: The former is a T-account, the latter is not
options.D: The former is not in the ledger, the latter is

questions.ai_explanation: Receipts and payments records cash movements when received or paid. Income and expenditure allocates income and expenses to the period to which they relate.
questions.explanation: Receipts and payments records cash movements when received or paid. Income and expenditure allocates income and expenses to the period to which they relate.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Club subscriptions: opening arrears₦40; closing arrears₦35; opening receipts in advance₦15; cash received₦2,560. With no closing advance, find subscription income.
questions.ai_explanation: Start with cash received ₦2,560. Subtract opening arrears ₦40, add closing arrears ₦35 and add opening receipts in advance ₦15. Income is ₦2,570.
questions.explanation: Start with cash received ₦2,560. Subtract opening arrears ₦40, add closing arrears ₦35 and add opening receipts in advance ₦15. Income is ₦2,570.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The net profit from the trading account of a non-profit making organization would be treated as income in the
questions.ai_explanation: A club’s trading activity produces a profit or loss separately. Its trading profit is then included as income in the club’s income and expenditure account.
questions.explanation: A club’s trading activity produces a profit or loss separately. Its trading profit is then included as income in the club’s income and expenditure account.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Ada contributes cash₦12,000, furniture₦18,000 and a vehicle₦70,000. Udo contributes cash₦10,000, a building₦5,000 and a computer₦135,000. Find total partnership capital.
questions.ai_explanation: Ada contributes ₦100,000 and Udo contributes ₦150,000. Adding the contributions gives the partnership’s total capital of ₦250,000.
questions.explanation: Ada contributes ₦100,000 and Udo contributes ₦150,000. Adding the contributions gives the partnership’s total capital of ₦250,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Ada contributes cash₦12,000, furniture₦18,000 and a vehicle₦70,000. Udo contributes cash₦10,000, a building₦5,000 and a computer₦135,000. If profits are shared in proportion to capital, find Ada:Udo’s ratio.
questions.ai_explanation: Their contributions are ₦100,000 and ₦150,000. The capital-based sharing ratio is 100,000:150,000, which reduces to 2:3 for Ada:Udo.
questions.explanation: Their contributions are ₦100,000 and ₦150,000. The capital-based sharing ratio is 100,000:150,000, which reduces to 2:3 for Ada:Udo.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The major distinguishing element between the final accounts of a partnership and a sole trader is the
questions.ai_explanation: The partnership appropriation account allocates profit among partners, including agreed interest and salaries. A sole trader has no profit allocation among multiple owners.
questions.explanation: The partnership appropriation account allocates profit among partners, including agreed interest and salaries. A sole trader has no profit allocation among multiple owners.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Authorised nominal capital₦50million is divided into100million shares.80million shares are issued fully paid at₦0.60 each. What is each share’s nominal value?
questions.ai_explanation: Nominal value per share is authorised nominal capital divided by the number of shares: ₦50million/100million = ₦0.50. The issue price is a separate amount.
questions.explanation: Nominal value per share is authorised nominal capital divided by the number of shares: ₦50million/100million = ₦0.50. The issue price is a separate amount.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Authorised nominal capital₦50million is divided into100million shares.80million shares are issued fully paid at₦0.60 each. What is issued nominal share capital?
questions.ai_explanation: Issued share capital uses nominal value: 80million × ₦0.50 = ₦40million. The additional ₦0.10 paid per share is share premium, not nominal share capital.
questions.explanation: Issued share capital uses nominal value: 80million × ₦0.50 = ₦40million. The additional ₦0.10 paid per share is share premium, not nominal share capital.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The document setting out theregulations regarding shares, meetings and internal organization of a company is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Articles of association contain rules for a company’s internal administration, such as share arrangements and meetings. A prospectus instead provides information for prospective investors.
questions.explanation: Articles of association contain rules for a company’s internal administration, such as share arrangements and meetings. A prospectus instead provides information for prospective investors.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An advantage of using accounting ratio is that they
questions.ai_explanation: Accounting ratios summarise relationships between figures, helping users compare performance and financial position and make decisions. They do not by themselves prove the absence of fraud.
questions.explanation: Accounting ratios summarise relationships between figures, helping users compare performance and financial position and make decisions. They do not by themselves prove the absence of fraud.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Gross sales₦219,900 less returns₦4,900 give net sales₦215,000. Opening and closing net receivables are₦20,000 and₦30,000. Treating these sales as credit sales, find receivables turnover.
questions.ai_explanation: Average receivables are (₦20,000 + ₦30,000)/2 = ₦25,000. Using net sales ₦215,000 as credit sales gives turnover 215,000/25,000 = 8.60 times per year.
questions.explanation: Average receivables are (₦20,000 + ₦30,000)/2 = ₦25,000. Using net sales ₦215,000 as credit sales gives turnover 215,000/25,000 = 8.60 times per year.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Sales are₦20,000 and cost of sales is₦15,000. Find gross profit margin.
questions.ai_explanation: Gross profit is sales less cost of sales, ₦20,000 − ₦15,000 = ₦5,000. Gross profit margin uses sales as the denominator, giving 5,000/20,000 × 100 = 25.00%.
questions.explanation: Gross profit is sales less cost of sales, ₦20,000 − ₦15,000 = ₦5,000. Gross profit margin uses sales as the denominator, giving 5,000/20,000 × 100 = 25.00%.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Department A: opening stock₦5,000,purchases₦26,000,closing stock₦7,000,sales₦45,000. Department B: opening stock₦1,500,purchases₦3,000,closing stock₦2,500,sales₦4,000. Rent₦8,300 and general expenses₦3,200 are allocated A:B=4:1. Find total gross profit.
questions.ai_explanation: A has cost of sales ₦24,000 and gross profit ₦21,000. B has cost of sales ₦2,000 and gross profit ₦2,000. Together the departments earn gross profit ₦23,000.
questions.explanation: A has cost of sales ₦24,000 and gross profit ₦21,000. B has cost of sales ₦2,000 and gross profit ₦2,000. Together the departments earn gross profit ₦23,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Department A: opening stock₦5,000,purchases₦26,000,closing stock₦7,000,sales₦45,000. Department B: opening stock₦1,500,purchases₦3,000,closing stock₦2,500,sales₦4,000. Rent₦8,300 and general expenses₦3,200 are allocated A:B=4:1. Find department B’s net result.
questions.ai_explanation: B’s gross profit is ₦4,000 − (₦1,500 + ₦3,000 − ₦2,500) = ₦2,000. Its one-fifth share of ₦11,500 expenses is ₦2,300, leaving a net loss of ₦300.
questions.explanation: B’s gross profit is ₦4,000 − (₦1,500 + ₦3,000 − ₦2,500) = ₦2,000. Its one-fifth share of ₦11,500 expenses is ₦2,300, leaving a net loss of ₦300.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The expenditure on a good or service which is consumed either immediately or within a current accounting period is called
questions.ai_explanation: Recurrent expenditure relates to goods and services consumed in ordinary current operations. It differs from capital expenditure, which creates or improves longer-lived assets.
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure relates to goods and services consumed in ordinary current operations. It differs from capital expenditure, which creates or improves longer-lived assets.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The receipts from a special tax levy to pay maturing interest obligation are recorded in
questions.ai_explanation: A debt service fund accounts for resources dedicated to paying debt principal and interest. A levy specifically intended for maturing interest therefore belongs to that fund.
questions.explanation: A debt service fund accounts for resources dedicated to paying debt principal and interest. A levy specifically intended for maturing interest therefore belongs to that fund.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The cash basis of accounting requires the recognition of revenue only when they are
questions.ai_explanation: Under the cash basis, revenue is recognised when cash is received. Earning an amount or making it due does not by itself trigger cash-basis recognition.
questions.explanation: Under the cash basis, revenue is recognised when cash is received. Earning an amount or making it due does not by itself trigger cash-basis recognition.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The amount for individual items on a government budget is called a
questions.ai_explanation: A vote is an amount authorised or allocated for an expenditure item in a government budget. It specifies the approved spending provision for that item.
questions.explanation: A vote is an amount authorised or allocated for an expenditure item in a government budget. It specifies the approved spending provision for that item.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The most important reason for studying accounting is that

options.A: the information provided by accounting is useful in making decisions
options.B: accounting plays an important role in a society
options.C: the study of accounting leads to a challenging career

questions.ai_explanation: Accounting supplies information that supports decisions about resources and performance. This decision usefulness is broader than simply calculating gross profit or offering a career.
questions.explanation: Accounting supplies information that supports decisions about resources and performance. This decision usefulness is broader than simply calculating gross profit or offering a career.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Creditors use accounting information for the purpose of
questions.ai_explanation: Creditors need to assess whether the business can meet its obligations when due. Liquidity information helps them evaluate that short-term payment capacity.
questions.explanation: Creditors need to assess whether the business can meet its obligations when due. Liquidity information helps them evaluate that short-term payment capacity.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The instruments that are generated when firms enter into business transactions with others are called
questions.ai_explanation: Source documents provide the initial evidence of a transaction, such as an invoice or credit note. Journals are accounting records prepared from that evidence.
questions.explanation: Source documents provide the initial evidence of a transaction, such as an invoice or credit note. Journals are accounting records prepared from that evidence.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Assets: motor van₦3,600,premises₦5,000,bank₦1,650,stock₦4,800,cash₦250,debtors₦6,910. Liabilities: loan₦1,000 and creditors₦2,560. Find capital.
questions.ai_explanation: Assets total ₦22,210. Deduct the ₦1,000 loan and ₦2,560 creditors to obtain owner’s capital: ₦22,210 − ₦3,560 = ₦18,650.
questions.explanation: Assets total ₦22,210. Deduct the ₦1,000 loan and ₦2,560 creditors to obtain owner’s capital: ₦22,210 − ₦3,560 = ₦18,650.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The document that is used to acknowledge the acceptance of the return of goods by the seller from the buyer is known as
questions.ai_explanation: A seller issues a credit note to acknowledge an accepted return and reduce the amount charged to the customer. It records the credit against the earlier sale.
questions.explanation: A seller issues a credit note to acknowledge an accepted return and reduce the amount charged to the customer. It records the credit against the earlier sale.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following transactions is BEST recorded in the general journal?

options.A: Payment of rent with a cheque.
options.C: Purchase of an asset on credit terms
options.D: Transfer of cash from head office to branch.

questions.ai_explanation: A non-current asset bought on credit is normally recorded in the general journal. Cash and cheque payments belong in the cash book, while inventory purchases use the purchases journal.
questions.explanation: A non-current asset bought on credit is normally recorded in the general journal. Cash and cheque payments belong in the cash book, while inventory purchases use the purchases journal.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The effects of the payment of a liability is that it
questions.ai_explanation: Paying a liability uses cash or bank, reducing an asset, and settles an amount owed, reducing a liability. Both sides of the accounting equation decrease equally.
questions.explanation: Paying a liability uses cash or bank, reducing an asset, and settles an amount owed, reducing a liability. Both sides of the accounting equation decrease equally.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An owner starts a business by depositing a₦500,000 cheque into its bank account. Which entries record this?

options.D: Debit owner’s account₦500,000; credit cheque account₦500,000

questions.ai_explanation: The owner’s cheque increases the business bank asset, which is debited. The corresponding increase in owner’s capital is credited for the same ₦500,000.
questions.explanation: The owner’s cheque increases the business bank asset, which is debited. The corresponding increase in owner’s capital is credited for the same ₦500,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which are advantages of an imprest petty cash system? I.Easier cheque drawing; II.Checks on cash use; III.Cash entrusted to the petty cashier is limited to the float; IV.Petty-cash losses can be minimised.
questions.ai_explanation: An imprest system establishes a fixed float, supports checks on spending and limits the cash entrusted to the petty cashier. These controls help minimise losses; easier cheque drawing is not its defining advantage.
questions.explanation: An imprest system establishes a fixed float, supports checks on spending and limits the cash entrusted to the petty cashier. These controls help minimise losses; easier cheque drawing is not its defining advantage.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening stock₦2,400;closing stock₦6,400;other expenses₦2,000;sales₦11,000;net profit₦900. Find purchases.
questions.ai_explanation: Net profit equals sales minus opening stock, purchases and expenses, plus closing stock. Rearranging gives purchases = ₦11,000 − ₦900 − ₦2,400 + ₦6,400 − ₦2,000 = ₦12,100.
questions.explanation: Net profit equals sales minus opening stock, purchases and expenses, plus closing stock. Rearranging gives purchases = ₦11,000 − ₦900 − ₦2,400 + ₦6,400 − ₦2,000 = ₦12,100.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Why are adjustments to the profit and loss account necessary?

options.A: To cover some expenses of the following year
options.B: To ascertain actual expenses incurred and income earned during the year
options.C: To show provisions made during the year
options.D: To show total expenses paid and income received during the year

questions.ai_explanation: Accrual and prepayment adjustments allocate income and expenses to the year they relate to. This allows the accounts to show the year’s actual income earned and expenses incurred.
questions.explanation: Accrual and prepayment adjustments allocate income and expenses to the year they relate to. This allows the accounts to show the year’s actual income earned and expenses incurred.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Machinery acquired1January1971 costs₦5,000,000,has residual value₦25,000 and useful life20years. Using straight-line depreciation from acquisition, find accumulated depreciation at31December1981.
questions.ai_explanation: Annual straight-line depreciation is (₦5,000,000 − ₦25,000)/20 = ₦248,750. From 1January1971 through 31December1981 is eleven years, giving accumulated depreciation ₦2,736,250.
questions.explanation: Annual straight-line depreciation is (₦5,000,000 − ₦25,000)/20 = ₦248,750. From 1January1971 through 31December1981 is eleven years, giving accumulated depreciation ₦2,736,250.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Fixed assets cost₦200,000 with accumulated depreciation₦100,000. Other assets:stock₦10,000,debtors₦4,500,bank₦22,800,cash₦9,700. The only liability,trade creditors,equals25%of capital. Find trade creditors.
questions.ai_explanation: Net assets before creditors total ₦147,000. Since creditors are one-quarter of capital, assets equal 1.25 times capital. Capital is ₦117,600 and creditors are ₦29,400.
questions.explanation: Net assets before creditors total ₦147,000. Since creditors are one-quarter of capital, assets equal 1.25 times capital. Capital is ₦117,600 and creditors are ₦29,400.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Fixed assets cost₦200,000 with accumulated depreciation₦100,000. Other assets:stock₦10,000,debtors₦4,500,bank₦22,800,cash₦9,700. The only liability,trade creditors,equals25%of capital. Find capital.
questions.ai_explanation: The asset total is ₦147,000. Writing creditors as 0.25C gives C + 0.25C = ₦147,000, so capital C = ₦147,000/1.25 = ₦117,600.
questions.explanation: The asset total is ₦147,000. Writing creditors as 0.25C gives C + 0.25C = ₦147,000, so capital C = ₦147,000/1.25 = ₦117,600.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The trial balance showed wages N 2,500 and a note stated that N500 wages were due but unpaid. When preparing final accounts and balance sheet, it is required to debit profit and loss account with

questions.question: Purchases ledger control:opening credit balance₦45,600;closing credit balance₦72,600;payments to suppliers₦437,000;discounts received₦18,600. Find credit purchases.
questions.ai_explanation: Closing creditors equal opening creditors plus credit purchases less payments and discounts. Purchases therefore equal ₦72,600 − ₦45,600 + ₦437,000 + ₦18,600 = ₦482,600.

questions.question: A retailer marks goods up25%on cost,has sales₦23,000,expenses10%of sales,and inventory turnover five times per year. Find average inventory at cost.
questions.ai_explanation: Cost of sales is ₦23,000/1.25 = ₦18,400. Inventory turnover equals cost of sales divided by average stock, so average stock is ₦18,400/5 = ₦3,680.

questions.question: A retailer marks goods up25%on cost,has sales₦23,000,expenses10%of sales,and inventory turnover five times per year. Find annual net profit.
questions.ai_explanation: Cost of sales is ₦18,400, giving gross profit ₦4,600. Expenses are 10% of ₦23,000, or ₦2,300. Net profit is ₦4,600 − ₦2,300 = ₦2,300.
